req_desc: The product presents a governed operator console for a serverless compute platform, with a public product page over the console ...
The stored role set is `owner`, `administrator`, `developer`, `operator`, `billing`, `read-only` ...
A seeded principal signs in with an email address, a password, reaching the workspace overview ...
Every console route carries the workspace before the environment, the environment before the resource ...
The apps list shows name, state, current version, function count, live container count, error rate, spend rate, last deploy ...
The containers surface lists identifier, function, version, state, age, accelerator class, memory, processor, utilisation, tasks served ...
A member holding `developer` files a request to promote a chosen version to the production environment ...
A member holding `operator` decides a promotion request that sits in `in-review`, supplying a reason ...
Approval of a promotion request changes no app version ...
A member holding `operator` rolls a production app back from the deployments list, supplying a reason ...
A secret is created with a name, a description, key pairs, value pairs ...
A machine token is created with a name, a scope set, a binding to one environment ...
A log query with no bound receives `422`, stating the narrowing that would be accepted ...
Every metered quantity is stored as an integer in a base unit, per task, per container ...
Every state transition is recorded with principal, action, resource, before value, after value, request identifier ...
A task links to the container of the task, to the log lines of the task, to the metrics window of the task ...
A privacy page is reachable from the footer of every public page ...
An unknown address renders the product's own not-found page, carrying a way back ...
Every form validates on blur, naming the field at fault, naming the fix ...
Navigation is a breadcrumbed drill-down from workspace, to environment, to resource, to tab ...
The interface is dark by default, carrying no light theme ...
Every route is rendered on the server, with interactive islands hydrating the streaming regions ...
A `principal` carries email, display name, status of `active`, `invited`, `deactivated` ...
The palette is authored as a raw layer naming physical ramps, a semantic layer naming ramps by job ...
No light theme is built ...
Schema, seed, `GET /api/health` land before any console route ...
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
core asks covered by this grader
